title: 2D Contour: with a Linear lead-in, the first descent stands on the cutter-centre line, before G41/G42 engages

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What happens

With a Linear lead-in and control or wear compensation, the plunge point of the first descent lies on the extension of the centre path. The tool edge is tangent to the finished wall at that point. The clearance to the wall is 0.000 mm. The descent runs before G41/G42 engages, so the posted program has no compensation at that move.

At nominal tool size the tool touches nothing at this point. A real tool larger than the nominal size would touch the wall. With a Perpendicular lead-in the same descent is one lead length away from the wall.

## Reading

Setup: Side Outside, entry Plunge, no transition, control and wear compensation, tool diameter 6 mm, stock to leave 0, top Z 0, bottom Z -4, stepdown 2, climb, lead length 3 mm. The part is three 16 mm squares, 30 mm apart. Clearance is the distance from the descent end points to the wall, minus the nominal radius (3.000 mm).

| Lead-in | Descents before G41/G42 | Least clearance to the wall |
|---|---|---|
| Linear 3 mm | 6 | 0.000 mm (all 6) |
| Perpendicular 3 mm | 6 | 3.000 mm (all 6) |

The result is the same for control and for wear compensation. The wall-side generator does not use the bore-side entry code, and this finding does not depend on a ring entry. The bore side (Side Inside) with a Linear lead-in reads 0.000 mm too, for Plunge and for Arc entry. It is the same on main.

## Where

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/arc_leads.rs:26-29`: `lead_in` returns the plunge point `s - t*length` for a Linear lead. That point is on the centre path's own edge. A Perpendicular lead returns `s + air*length` (lines 22-25).
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_comp.rs`: `door` and `push_span`. The span starts at the lead-in move. The moves before it are G40, at the nominal centre.
- `docs/decisions/3888-ramp-comp-refusal.md:23-26`: "The dive at the lead-in's start, which the door's lead-length law keeps at least one radius off the ring, stays legal."

The premise of that sentence holds for a Perpendicular lead-in (3.000 mm). It does not hold for a Linear lead-in (0.000 mm). The sentence is not about a Linear lead-in, and no other file says that the 0.000 mm is by design.

## Not known

I did not measure a real tool larger than the register value on a machine. The reading is from the generated path only.

## Expected

One of these:
- The descent for a Linear lead-in stands at least some stated distance off the wall, as for a Perpendicular lead-in.
- Or the decision file and the lead-in documentation state that a Linear lead-in descent is tangent to the wall, so a user can choose a Perpendicular lead-in.

## Done means

- A test with a Linear lead-in and control compensation names the least clearance of the descents before the first G41/G42, and pins the chosen rule.
- The decision file for #3888 states the rule for both lead-in types.

Refs #3888, #3890.
